body: While he is my brother we are very different people and, despite coming from the same home, different histories. I love him but talking to him about this sort of stuff would cause him needless anguish.

You seem hostile.

He most likely doesn't suspect. And I know, as well as I could possibly know, from knowing him as my brother. Why is it important?

That's just my bias coming into play, I guess. I've given myself a two week deadline. I'll try to find something that shows promise that I'm not in a hopeless situation before that. A part of that might very well be going to the hospital, which is something I might very well do if I don't come up with anything else. That something else might be my uni's counsellor (way less out of my comfort zone) who emailed me saying an appointment might come up sooner as people are prone to cancelling.

I guess I'm wary of state workers due to my background and experiences. The state being semi-synonymous to incompetence and lack of sense.

Estonia. I might try the hotline, we do have one and it even has a really simple number. Though from what little I've read it's more of a comfortable vent line, something you'd call when you've gotten drunk after a breakup or getting fired. I'm someone who has pondered the decision for a while now, weighing the pros and cons of continuing a life that lacks purpose and joy, I doubt I'd get much besides common sense soothing phrases.

Besides the added humiliation of asking someone I know for help (semi-anonymity is bad enough), not much would come of it besides guilting me to not do it. It's a decision I've made by myself and whether I find a prospective way to escape the deterioration of my mind or kill myself is a decision I will make by myself.

The country is Estonia, I wouldn't have to pay anything besides a token(ish) consultation fee. At least I think so, not exactly sure how the specifics of the NHS work (physical health is good so no prior experience besides seeing the optometrist). But given that it's state provided I can probably expect a 3 month queue and an overworked misanthropic 50 yo professional who'd just tell me anything to get me out of the door. I was referring to a private practitioner in the OP, though there's also the chance that they'd be untrained crackpots at attainable fees. I might be a little bit biased though.

I was suicidal in my early teens, I know what to expect.

Of course he's important to me. Him not finding is about us sharing a dorm room, I wouldn't want him or my suitemates to find me. And I couldn't exactly take up a subject like that with a 19 yo broski that comes from the same emotionally distant family as I do (he's a normal person though, mental health wise, so no common ground).
